records.title: Continuity
records.definition: Keeping an essential function operating through a named owner, backup, review time, and escalation route.

records.title: CPR
records.definition: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: chest compressions, with rescue breaths when trained and willing, used when a person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.

records.title: Deployer
records.definition: The person who adapts, prints, places, checks, and maintains a local copy of the guide.

records.title: Dispatcher
records.definition: The trained call handler in a control centre who gathers information, sends suitable help, and may coach immediate actions.

records.title: Interoception
records.definition: Processing signals from inside the body, including sensing, attention, interpretation, prediction, and regulation.

records.title: Public reference ID
records.definition: A stable typed address such as [BEG:C:S:004]. The ID stays stable even when page numbers or surrounding sections move.

records.title: Reader
records.definition: Any person using the guide in the moment; the reader is never assumed to be the deployer.

records.title: Recovery position
records.definition: A stable side-lying position used for an unresponsive person who is breathing normally when movement is not prevented by major trauma.

records.title: Red flag
records.definition: A sign or situation that overrides ordinary self-care and changes the route to urgent or emergency help.

records.title: Source limit
records.definition: The boundary of what a source, study, protocol, or model can honestly establish.

records.title: Triage
records.definition: Prioritizing action by urgency and likely harm; in this guide it is a lay routing aid, not a clinical diagnosis.

records.title: Vital sign
records.definition: An observation such as breathing, pulse, temperature, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, or glucose that may help a handoff but cannot by itself clear a red flag.
